q: בן 85 עם רקע רפואי של אי ספיקת לב, COPD, סוכרת ויתר לחץ דם מתקבל למחלקה סיעודית. לאחר בירור מול המשפחה ורופא המשפחה – לא ברור האם קיבל חיסון לפנאומוקוק בעברו. מה ההמלצה לגבי ההתחסנות לפנואומוקוק עבור המטופל?
o: יש להתחסן ב-PCV13 (PREVENAR) בלבד
אם יש ספק בעניין חיסון קודם מותר לתת חיסון חוזר
אין חשיבות לחיסון בגיל 85 באם לא חוסן עד כה
באם סבל מדלקת ריאות ב-5 שנים האחרונות, יש לתת חיסון PCV13 ו-PPSV23
explanation:
Pneumococcal vaccination prevents invasive disease in older adults with chronic heart or lung disease. At age 85, **offer vaccination if the history remains unknown** after checking records.

**A. PCV13 alone** — A 13-valent vaccine alone is not the current Israeli approach. Israel replaced this conjugate product with PCV20.
**B. Vaccinate when prior receipt is uncertain** — Uncertainty after checking the available history is a reason to use the schedule for unknown status. A documented prior series calls for its own interval and product review.
**C. Age 85 makes vaccination unnecessary** — Age, COPD, heart failure and diabetes increase his risk of serious pneumococcal illness.
**D. Two vaccines after any recent pneumonia** — A previous pneumonia could have had many causes. Vaccine selection depends on age, risk and prior vaccine products and dates.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 165, 1690. Israel Ministry of Health, pneumococcal vaccine for older adults, 19 November 2025. CDC Adult Immunization Schedule Notes, pneumococcal vaccination.
Key note: The printed 8e pneumococcal vaccine sequence is discussed on pp165 and 1690. The current Israeli and CDC recommendations cited above have a separate source.

q: גבר יפני בן 81 מגיע לביקורת שגרתית. הוא מעשן 2 קופסאות ביום במשך 60 שנה ואינו מעוניין להפסיק. בתו שואלת מדוע פער תוחלת החיים בין גברים לנשים ביפן לא הצטמצם כמו במדינות מפותחות אחרות. מה מסביר בצורה הטובה ביותר את הדפוס המתמשך הזה?
o: עומס תעסוקתי גבוה יותר אצל הגברים.
מדיניות בריאות המקנה לנשים קדימות בטיפול.
פער ממושך בשיעורי העישון בין נשים לגברים.
הבדלים גנטיים המסבירים את השינוי בין הדורות.
explanation:
**שכיחות עישון נמוכה היסטורית בקרב נשים ביפן מול חשיפה גבוהה בגברים** שמרה על פער בתמותה המיוחסת לטבק באותם דורות.

**א. עומס תעסוקתי גבוה יותר אצל הגברים** — עומס תעסוקתי עשוי להשפיע על הבריאות, אך אינו הדפוס ההיסטורי המובא בהשוואה.
**ב. מדיניות בריאות המקנה לנשים קדימות בטיפול** — השאלה עוסקת בהבדל ממושך בחשיפות ולא ניתנת בה עדות להעדפה במערכת הבריאות.
**ג. פער ממושך בשיעורי העישון בין נשים לגברים** — שכיחות העישון נותרה נמוכה בנשים יפניות לעומת גברים במשך זמן רב. זו החשיפה הנבחנת כאן.
**ד. הבדלים גנטיים המסבירים את השינוי בין הדורות** — הסבר גנטי לבדו אינו מסביר את הקשר בין דפוסי עישון משתנים והפער בין הדורות.

אסמכתא · Hazzard 8e, פרק 5, עמ׳ 85–87.
ref: Hazzard Ch 5 — SEX DIFFERENCES IN HEALTH AND LONGEVITY
chapterTitle: Sex Differences in Health and Longevity

q: An older patient with advanced kidney dysfunction has cognitive impairment that may represent either advanced dementia or uremia-induced delirium. What does this uncertainty mean for the dialysis discussion?
o: Consider withholding dialysis because the impairment favors a diagnosis of irreversible dementia
Consider maintenance dialysis because response-based reassessment adds little to the treatment decision
Consider a dialysis trial because uremic delirium remains a plausible explanation
Consider waiting for cognitive recovery before using dialysis to address uremic delirium
explanation:
Uremic delirium is cognitive dysfunction caused by advanced kidney failure and can improve with dialysis. When it mimics advanced dementia, **a time-limited dialysis trial with agreed goals and reassessment** can help determine whether treatment benefits this person.

**A. Withhold dialysis on the assumption of dementia** — Confusion during advanced kidney failure may have a reversible component. Establish the prior course and consider a trial when the distinction remains uncertain.
**B. Commit to maintenance dialysis without reassessment** — The value of a trial lies in assessing cognition, function and treatment burden before deciding on maintenance therapy.
**C. Offer a trial because uremic delirium is plausible** — Agree on observable goals and review timing with the patient or surrogate. Clearing uremic symptoms may take several weeks.
**D. Wait for cognitive recovery before treating uremia** — If accumulated toxins are driving the delirium, waiting for spontaneous improvement leaves the possible cause untreated.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1291, 1293, Contraindications to Renal Replacement Therapy and Time-Limited Trial of Dialysis.

q: An 86-year-old woman has severe osteoarthritis involving all compartments of the knee. Persistent pain limits walking and social participation despite maximal pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic treatment. She is medically fit for surgery and wishes to discuss it. Which intervention is best supported?
o: Arthroscopic debridement with lavage of the knee joint
Intra-articular injection of platelet-rich plasma
Realignment through a high tibial osteotomy
Total replacement of the knee joint
explanation:
When all knee compartments are affected, shifting load from one compartment to another leaves substantial disease in the weight-bearing joint. **Total knee replacement is the supported operation for this fit patient with persistent disabling symptoms.**

**A. Debridement and lavage** — Arthroscopy for degenerative knee OA generally provides no better symptom relief than a sham procedure.
**B. Platelet-rich plasma** — Injection protocols vary, and evidence does not support using this as a substitute for indicated arthroplasty.
**C. High tibial osteotomy** — This is intended for selected varus knees with predominantly medial disease and a healthier opposite compartment.
**D. Total knee replacement** — It addresses the whole joint. Discuss expected gains in walking and pain alongside complications, recovery and residual symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 789–790, Surgical interventions.

. Total knee replacement** — It addresses the whole joint. Discuss expected gains in walking and pain alongside complications, recovery and residual symptoms.

q: A 77-year-old man in rehabilitation after hip-fracture repair has constant pain at rest and with movement. As-needed immediate-release oxycodone relieves it, but late administration allows pain to recur between doses. Which dosing strategy fits this pain pattern in Hazzard?
o: Administer the medication after the pain has peaked each time
Concentrate medication administration at night despite daytime pain
Reserve medication administration for the daytime physiotherapy sessions
Plan scheduled administration and titrate treatment to comfort
explanation:
Pain persisting at rest has a different dosing requirement from brief pain with therapy. **Scheduled, individually titrated analgesia can prevent predictable gaps in relief.**

**A. Administer the medication after the pain has peaked each time** Waiting for peak pain allows repeated suffering and can undermine rehabilitation.
**B. Concentrate medication administration at night despite daytime pain** Concentrating doses overnight leaves daytime baseline and movement pain untreated.
**C. Reserve medication administration for the daytime physiotherapy sessions** Dosing only for therapy misses pain at rest.
**D. Plan scheduled administration and titrate treatment to comfort** Schedule treatment to match the pattern, reassess alertness and function, and reduce scheduled dosing as acute pain resolves.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Table 68-6, p. 1061.

o: הזנה בזונדה כחלופה קבועה לאכילה
הזנה דרך PEG בגלל הירידה הקוגניטיבית

**א. הזנה בזונדה כחלופה קבועה לאכילה.** זונדה מוסיפה התערבות בלי צורך שהודגם כאן.

q: An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced dementia and breast cancer metastatic to bone presents with two days of shouting, agitation, food refusal, and pulling at her clothes. She is nonverbal at baseline and grimaces during abdominal palpation. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, heart rate 88, and blood pressure 142/78. She receives memantine 10 mg twice daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. Which approach best addresses the acute behavioral change?
o: Escalate analgesia and defer investigation of the abdominal findings
Start an antipsychotic and defer assessment of medical triggers
Evaluate medical contributors with examination and targeted testing
Increase scheduled acetaminophen and defer assessment of medical triggers
explanation:
In advanced dementia, new shouting, refusal and grimacing may be the only outward signs of acute illness or pain. An abdominal finding gives the assessment direction.
**Examine for medical precipitants and obtain targeted testing consistent with her goals.**

**A. Escalate analgesia and defer investigation of the abdominal findings.** Analgesia may be needed now, but increasing it alone could mask a new abdominal disorder.
**B. Start an antipsychotic and defer assessment of medical triggers.** Antipsychotic treatment before evaluating distress risks missing pain or other treatable illness.
**C. Evaluate medical contributors with examination and targeted testing.** The focal pain behavior can guide an examination even when a verbal history is impossible.
**D. Increase scheduled acetaminophen and defer assessment of medical triggers.** More acetaminophen is not a substitute for assessing the cause and severity of new tenderness.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 885, 890

q: A patient with chronic hemolytic anemia is asymptomatic at a baseline hemoglobin of 6 g/dL. A target of 7 g/dL is being considered. What consequence does the example in Hazzard describe?
o: More frequent transfusions with improved quality of life
Less frequent transfusions with improved quality of life
Less frequent transfusions without improved quality of life
More frequent transfusions without improved quality of life
explanation:
Raising a chronic transfusion target increases the amount of donor blood needed to maintain it. Whether that burden is worthwhile depends on symptoms and function at the patient's usual hemoglobin.

**In this asymptomatic example, raising the goal from 6 to 7 g/dL brings more frequent transfusions without better quality of life.**

**A. More transfusions and better quality of life.** More transfusions are plausible, but the vignette supplies no symptom that the higher target relieves.
**B. Fewer transfusions and better quality of life.** Maintaining a higher target tends to increase transfusion requirements, with no benefit demonstrated in this example.
**C. Fewer transfusions and unchanged quality of life.** The quality-of-life observation fits, but the predicted transfusion frequency runs in the wrong direction.
**D. More transfusions and unchanged quality of life.** The higher target imposes extra visits and exposures without improving the outcome the patient experiences.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.

chapterTitle: AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA

q: למי מהמטופלים הבאים מתאים להיעזר ברולטור?
o: בת 72 הסובלת מ- Lewy Body Dementia
בן 77, שמור קוגניטיבית, לאחר שבץ, סובל מפרזיס ביד ורגל ימין
בן 85 הסובל ממחלת פרקינסון
בת 88 הסובלת מ- Pulmonary Fibrosis וקוצר נשימה במאמץ
explanation:
A rollator is a wheeled walker with hand brakes and usually a seat. It can help when endurance limits walking because the person can rest without searching for a chair. **The woman with pulmonary fibrosis and exertional dyspnea has the clearest reason to try one, provided she demonstrates safe steering, braking and transfers.**

**A. Lewy body dementia.** Attention and visuospatial fluctuations may compromise brake use. Assess actual ability rather than excluding everyone with this diagnosis.
**B. Right-sided paresis.** Arm weakness may affect steering or bilateral brake control. Test his support needs and device control directly.
**C. Parkinson disease.** Freezing and postural instability can make a freely rolling frame unsafe. Device selection depends on observed gait and supervision.
**D. Pulmonary fibrosis.** Rest breaks could address breath-limited walking. During a supervised trial, observe whether she stops, locks the brakes, turns and sits or rises safely.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 827–828, Table 55-5.

q: Which patient group matches the FDA-approved indication for memantine (Namenda) stated in Hazzard 8e?
o: Patients diagnosed with Alzheimer disease of any severity
Patients diagnosed with moderate to severe Alzheimer disease
Patients diagnosed with the mild cognitive impairment syndrome
Patients diagnosed with Alzheimer disease of mild severity
explanation:
Memantine reduces excessive NMDA receptor activity and is a symptomatic medication. The approved indication specifies Alzheimer dementia and a particular severity range.

**Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer dementia** is the patient group matching that indication.

**A. Alzheimer disease at any severity.** This would extend the indication to mild disease and earlier biological stages.
**B. Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer disease.** At this stage memantine can offer modest benefits in cognition, daily activities or behavior.
**C. Mild cognitive impairment.** MCI retains functional independence. Memantine has no established preventive indication for this syndrome.
**D. Mild Alzheimer disease.** Mild dementia falls earlier than the approved severity range for memantine.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 896, 911.

q: מה ההבדל בין Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) לבין Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS) בזקנים?
o: המרכיב של החמצת משנית לגופי הקטון גדול יותר ב- HHS
המרכיב של ההתייבשות הוא משמעותי יותר ב- HHS ומשנית לכך פגיעה כלייתית
האטיולוגיה של HHS בניגוד ל- DKA היא בעיקר של חוסר באינסולין שמוביל לליפוליזה ולחמצת
בקשישים שבריריים בני 80 ומעלה DKA שכיח יותר מ- HHS
keySource: IMA 2023-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q114
explanation:
In diabetic ketoacidosis, severe insulin deficiency triggers lipolysis, ketone production and acidosis. In hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state, sustained glycosuria can cause extreme water loss.

**Dehydration and secondary renal impairment are especially prominent in HHS.** This syndrome occurs predominantly in older people and may cause altered consciousness with few ketones.

**A. Greater ketoacidosis in HHS.** Ketoacid accumulation defines DKA.
**B. Greater dehydration and renal impairment in HHS.** Osmotic urine losses reduce kidney perfusion and further constrain glucose clearance.
**C. Lipolysis and ketoacidosis as the principal cause of HHS.** This describes DKA. Ketosis in HHS is usually modest or absent.
**D. DKA predominates in frail people over 80.** HHS is characteristic of older patients, although DKA can occur, particularly in type 1 diabetes.
